51: ## Optional declarations, install/launch and rollback
52: 
53: Draft.2's closed `/context` and `contextGrants` shapes have no per-selection optional flag. A caller cannot add `required: false` to those arrays/values and claim compatibility. The approved next schema may explicitly express optional selections. Only a declared supported schema representation can exclude an unsupported optional request with an `optional-unsupported` field diagnostic and requested/excluded/effective receipt entry. Legacy nonempty selections remain required by default; no blanket optional downgrade.
54: 
55: Delivery A installs these diagnostics at executable binding/member preflight and rechecks them at launch against current capability; team-package preflight must inspect the actual member definitions rather than admit solely from a service capability bit. Pending/runnable attempts with old bindings do not bypass unsupported semantics. Empty legacy declarations remain narrow and need no background migration. Planning/import/export preserves immutable definitions even when executable activation is refused.
56: 
57: Operator remediation sequence: inspect exact pointer and installed definition/package/binding revision; choose to preserve the requirement and wait, or deliberately author a new compatible immutable version; recompute canonical/exact-byte digests and lock closure; preflight against the chosen runtime profile; explicitly install/rebind with expected revision; inspect requested/effective/excluded receipt and localized Boss guidance before admitting work. Never overwrite the same immutable ID/version with a different digest, silently revise historical receipts, erase external effects, or tell the operator to delete storage. A compatible rollback is another explicit rebind and does not reverse already issued effects.
58: 
59: The uncomfortable limitation is deliberate: a definition that previously appeared executable while its nonempty resource selection was ignored may now refuse. That change protects the declared task contract. The implementation/release must publish these exact field dispositions; source implementation is not evidence that packaged refusals or their UI have operated.
64: Delivery A installs field-specific required-unsupported diagnostics in team binding preflight and admission. The parent lead recorded Gate A passing before authorizing Delivery B; its canonical operation receipt is the authority for that result. Delivery B additions are not yet certified by this document, and installed customer acceptance remains separate. Retained legacy attempts without an execution fence or captured endpoint settings require explicit reconciliation and are never silently upgraded.
65: 
66: ## Catalog authority and recovery
67: 
68: The catalog holds one nonexpiring execution claim with catalog, stable service, generated incarnation and epoch identities. CAS transitions hold, drain and release the claim; elapsed time or a new process never authorizes takeover. Admissions capture the execution fence and effective provider/model/profile/settings identities. Binding preflight, dispatch, actual effect authorization, durable mutation and recovery compare the current fence. A changed provider setting requires explicit rebind, not a silently adopted setting.
69: 
70: Authenticated host administration additionally requires the configured admin key. The owner view is available at `GET /api/v1/collaboration/execution-owner`. `POST /execution-owner/quiesce` stops admission, cancels and joins the exact owned runtime jobs and their actor roots/children, then records an internal `trusted-runtime-joined` fencing receipt. Unknown already-issued effects stay uncertain and reservations remain held; a stop proof does not certify them. Full process shutdown releases ownership only after global resource cleanup succeeds.
71: 
72: `POST /execution-owner/reclaim` consumes an existing internally recorded fencing receipt, expected epoch, operator reason and fresh replacement incarnation. A caller-supplied string or Boolean cannot create that proof. Reclaim preserves queued attempt/run/task/member IDs, the original admitted fence, effective settings and reservation; an explicit transfer record supplies the new execution fence. Successful results keep their output/dependency readiness even when accounting is unknown.
73: 
74: The fixed host-only `POST /team-instances/{team}/tasks/{task}/admit-queued` accepts the ordinary admission request but leaves its intent undispatched. `POST /team-instances/{team}/attempts/{attempt}/dispatch` accepts `{commandId, expectedTeamRevision}`, records an idempotent dispatch command and invokes the existing controller.
